clue.text: Me a helper? Beat it! My life's too short

indicators.note: to beat something is to batter it out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A would-be assistant is sent packing by someone with no time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat it!' reads as a dismissal but tells you to shuffle MEAHELPER. The definition is what a short-lived thing might say of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Something short-lived could fairly lament that its life lasts too briefly; that transience is the adjective's meaning.

clue.text: Hospital department wants one to be dependent completely

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
I is the Roman numeral one
to rely on is to be dependent on

explanation.surface: A hospital department needs someone to lean on entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: doing something wholly or totally is doing it in full.

clue.text: Hankering to burst into some laughter — one does

indicators.note: one word bursting into another sits inside it

parts.note: HA is a single laugh, a bit of laughter
a yen is a longing or hankering

explanation.surface: Someone longs to break out laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one does' completes the surface: an animal that laughs, as the spotted species is said to.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted animal is famous for a cackling call likened to laughter, so it is one that laughs.

clue.text: Don't change horses here, hemmed in by papers

parts.note: to be in the midst of things is to be surrounded or hemmed in by them
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: Advice not to swap mounts, given by someone buried in paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'don't change horses in midstream' means not altering course halfway through a task.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the proverb warns against swapping horses halfway across a river, so that place is where you should not switch.

clue.text: Musing of cleric upset republic

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a cleric

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland

explanation.surface: Reflections of a priest who is troubled by a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a daydream or state of quiet reflection is a musing.

clue.text: Is it reasonable to be private in public house?

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the local is one's nearby pub
a GI is a US private soldier

explanation.surface: A question about whether one can keep things private in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something sensible and soundly argued is reasonable.

clue.text: Own the lot? Own not quite all

parts.note: the lot means everything, all

indicators.note: not quite all of a word means its last letter is missing

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A question of whether one owns everything or just most of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite all' docks the final N of the second 'Own', leaving OW.
explanation.definitionFit: To own in the sense of admit or concede means to grant that something is so.

clue.text: Exhausted, with everything included

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a colloquial word for worn out, and a phrase describing a price that covers every extra.

clue.text: Where a murderer took refuge in sleep

definitions.meaning: in Genesis Cain, having killed Abel, went to dwell east of Eden in this region
a jocular phrase for the state of slumber

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the biblical place of Cain's exile, and by a pun on nodding off, the realm of slumber.

clue.text: Question posed about mistake made by boat

indicators.note: the question is placed around the other piece

parts.note: why is a question word
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone asks about an error made by a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'posed about' tells you the question word goes round the other piece; the noun 'mistake' must become a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a light rowing boat, especially one ferrying passengers on a river, is this kind of craft.

clue.text: Cloth produced by pretty daughter

parts.note: twee means affectedly pretty or quaint

explanation.surface: Fabric made by an attractive girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a rough woollen fabric, often from Scotland, is a cloth.

clue.text: Self-appointed upholder of the law leaving it in ruins

indicators.note: something in ruins is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who takes the law into their own hands leaves wreckage behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: a person who enforces justice without official authority.

clue.text: Plan for duty to cover article such as cooker

indicators.note: the first piece covers or encloses the second

parts.note: a roster is a schedule of duties
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A duty plan that includes, say, a cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such as' is a link: the answer is one example of a cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an oven or pan for roasting meat is a kind of cooker.

clue.text: Prison forbidding openness

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
dour means stern and forbidding

explanation.surface: A jail forbids frankness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forbidding' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning grim.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: frankness and honesty in speech amount to openness.

clue.text: Permission to approach water supply by oneself, but touch nothing

parts.note: leave means permission, as in leave to speak
a well supplies water
alone means by oneself

explanation.surface: Someone allowed to go to the well alone is told not to touch anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase means not to interfere with something that is satisfactory as it is.

clue.text: Next to lodge is an unusual construction

indicators.note: words given an unusual construction are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Beside a lodge stands an odd building.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is all three words 'lodge is an'; 'unusual construction' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something placed beside another is next to it.

clue.text: Sale he arranged on ageing property that's let

indicators.note: letters arranged are put into a new order

parts.note: something ageing is old

explanation.surface: A sale organised for an old rented house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: in a down clue the OLD piece simply sits on top of, i.e. after, the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: property held under a lease rather than owned outright is let to the holder.

clue.text: Imprisoned in America, ready for release

definitions.meaning: the can is US slang for jail, so this means locked up
film people use the phrase for a finished film ready to go out

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: American slang for being in jail, and film-making jargon for a completed picture.

clue.text: Public land's coloured yellow; private land is not distinguished

parts.note: a common is public land open to all
or is gold or yellow in heraldry
a garden is a private plot of land

explanation.surface: A park painted yellow next to a private plot, nothing special.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase means ordinary or unremarkable.

clue.text: Knox's partner going to America, full of trepidation

parts.note: Jimmy Nervo partnered Teddy Knox in a British comedy double act of the Crazy Gang era
US is short for the United States

explanation.surface: A performer's stage partner, nervous about a trip to America.
explanation.walkthrough: Nervo and Knox were a British music-hall comedy duo in the Crazy Gang of the 1930s.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being anxious and apprehensive is being full of trepidation.

clue.text: Cheese displayed in Capri cottage

indicators.note: the answer is on show inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Cheese is on display in a holiday cottage on an Italian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a soft Italian whey cheese is one kind of cheese.

clue.text: Press suffer defeat in court

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to lose is to suffer defeat

explanation.surface: Newspapers are beaten in a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalists, but here it is a cupboard, a sense common in Scotland and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a press is an old or regional word for a cupboard, which is a small storage room.

clue.text: Vessel with less tonnage

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used to load or unload ships
weighing less, the comparative of light

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a barge for transferring cargo, and the comparative of an adjective meaning not heavy.

clue.text: See Oliver dance

definitions.meaning: Oliver is the orphan in a Dickens novel whose surname you are pointed to
a 1960s dance involving swivelling the hips

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the surname of the Dickens orphan Oliver, and a 1960s dance craze.

clue.text: He's rich, after relocating treasure

indicators.note: letters relocated are moved into new positions

parts.note: a possessive or contracted 's gives an S here, as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A wealthy man moves house in search of riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treasure' is a verb here, not the hoard the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to prize or value dearly is to treasure.

clue.text: Opening bars is not that risky only initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the words in front of it

explanation.surface: Playing the first bars of music is not that dangerous at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the opening passage of a song or piece is its introduction.

clue.text: Snippets of information kept back by one racing spy: "Tell me forthwith!"

indicators.note: kept back here means turned back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: tips are useful snippets of information
I is the Roman numeral one
a tout spies on racehorses in training to sell information

explanation.surface: A racecourse informant withholds tips and is urged to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept back' turns TIPS into SPIT. A TOUT in racing watches horses' trials to sell tips.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase is an impatient demand to say something at once.

clue.text: First sign of pain penetrating in ear or in eye

indicators.note: one piece penetrates, going inside the other

parts.note: otic means relating to the ear

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A pain that pierces either the ear or the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the adjective means relating to the eye or vision, as in the nerve serving sight.

clue.text: Crime solved by the Yard, in part

parts.note: a foot, FT, is part of a yard

explanation.surface: A crime cleared up by Scotland Yard, at least partly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Yard' suggests Scotland Yard, London's police; in fact a foot is a third of a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: stealing is a crime.

clue.text: Leave the witness box and resign

definitions.meaning: a witness is told to step down when finished
to quit a post or withdraw

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the courtroom instruction to a finished witness, and quitting an office.
